findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employee was observed not using a barrier to shut the faucet after handwashing. PIC was made aware and education carried out. Ensure that employees are reminded to always use a barrier to shut the faucet after handwashing handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Employee was observed bare handling slices of ready to eat bread and pizza. Education was carried out. Employee donned gloves appropriately. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable about not bare handling ready to eat food items before serving.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple container of white powders on storage shelves in one of the prep area. Inquiries were made and education carried out. The containers were label appropriately. Ensure that containers holding white powders of any kind are properly labeled.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The internal surface of the microwave was observed with an accumulation of soil and food debris. PIC was made aware. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces of equipments that are exposed to splash and spillage are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Sanitizer bucket tested at 0 ppm during inspection. PIC was made aware and PIC had the Sani bucket remade. Ensure that the sanitizer in the sani bucket is tested at a regular frequency to ensure that sanitizer remain at the appropriate concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Sanitizer bucket tested at 0 ppm during inspection. PIC was made aware and PIC had the Sani bucket remade. Ensure that the sanitizer in the sani bucket is tested at a regular frequency to ensure that sanitizer remain at the appropriate concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed visible light coming through the back exit door located in the dish room area. PIC was made aware and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs would be done to have the door sealed properly. Ensure that entries and exits of the facility are completely sealed when closed to prevent the entry of rodents and other pest.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Inspector observed the employee bathroom in the middle basement to be lacking a supply of hand towels. Towels were provided to the bathroom. The violation is considered corrected on site.

Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: Inspector observed a container of spaghetti in the process of cooling with at tight fitting lid. Best practice is to loosely cover or leave cooling foods uncovered (see part B). 

(A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee wash hands and then turn off the faucet without using a barrier. Employee was stopped and coached on proper hand washing procedures. Take every opportunity to coach hand washing practices. The violaiton is considered corrected on site. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the black chest freezer to be encrusted with ice. Defrost freezer and maintain it smooth and cleanable.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the caulk seal in the restroom off of the back dining area to be soiled. Replace the caulk seal on this sink.  
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Hand towels were out at the main hand sink. Inspector was able to take paper towels from the coffee bare area and finish washing hands. The towels were replaced without direction from the inspector.  Violations was corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

Take care when cooling foods. Pan of red sauce was in the cooler with a tight fitting lid. The facility does a lot of cooling. Ensure that items are cooling properly by loosely covering them during the cooling period to allow the heat to move out of the food. Cooling foods were in the unit at 56F and had been cooling since prepared this morning.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Inspector observed a bottle of ibuprofen on the counter at the coffee bar area. The bottle was removed to an area by the hand sink that is an acceptable location. The violation is corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed bulk sausage in the pizza prep table top at 47.5 F when probed with a thermometer. The top of the sausage was far above the cold holding line of the unit. Facility states that the sausage was not left in the prep top over night. Food in the pan was taken down to the cold holding line and the remainder of the bulk sausage temped out at 40F when probed with a digital probe thermometer. Take care to store foods properly protected and cold held.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

Observed two bottles of cleaner stored hanging off of the edge of a cart holding clean kitchen utensils. The bottles were removed and the utensils are observed clean and dry. Store chemicals properly. Bottles were removed to the chemical storage area.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed ladles at the soup area and spoons used to stir sauces on the stove top stored on surfaces next to food. Store in use utensils properly.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
REPEAT
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Allergen awareness certificate is expired. Renew allergen training and have second food manager take allergen training. Supply certificates to binder by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed employee to wash hands with gloves still on. Proper hand washing was noted (with a barrier used to turn off the faucet handles); however, gloves must be discarded, appropriate hand washing completed, and new gloves should be donned. Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure staff is aware washing gloves while still wearing the gloves is not allowed. Cease practice. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed employee to ring a sanitization rag, followed by turning on faucets, running rag under water, then ringing rag again into the hand washing sink. Proceed to sanitize surfaces of meat slicer. Cease practice. Hand washing sinks are for hand washing ONLY. No other use for these sinks. Rags should not be wrung in hand washing sinks. Rags should be rung and come straight from the sani buckets (with appropriate concentrations of sanitizer in buckets). Discussed with PIC and employee. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed multiple chest freezers to have an accumulation of frost and ice. Ensure staff is aware to routinely defrost freezers to hinder accumulation of frost and ice. Discussed with PIC. Ensure defrosting of freezers by next routine inspection - smooth material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed Nudo board nailed to the 3 compartment sink/dish machine wall but no caulk around the Nudo board edges and the wall - not smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure caulking around the Nudo board to the wall in this area. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed all allergen training certifications to be expired. One CFPM did not have allergen training completed. Provided information sheet regarding where to obtain training and certification. Ensure all certified food protection manager’s have allergen training certification. Expires every 3 years. Ensure completed and copies in public health binder by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed soda nozzles at the front customer area to be soiled. Discussed with PIC. Ensure food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. 

Observed no probe thermometer for the facility. Facility has a digital surface thermometer for food. Discussed with PIC. Facility should have a thermometer than can measure the temperature of thin masses of proteins. Inspector will follow-up on 3/14/22.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple plates next to the pizza ovens to not be protected against cross contamination. Discussed the need to invert plates so food- and lip-contact surfaces are not exposed. Ensure staff is aware.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed frost on all chest freezers, but mainly on the small miniature chest freezer near the salad prep area in the kitchen. Ensure routine cleaning of NonFOOD-contact surfaces. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/24/21.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed employee to dump low sanitization bucket of bleach into kitchen hand sink. Discussed that hand sinks are for handwashing only. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

(REPEAT) Observed several areas of the facility (pizza prep area and drying dish area) where clean dish ware and/or cookware are being placed right-side up and thus not in protection from cross contamination. Discussed with PIC. Cease practice. This is a repeat violation from the last two routine inspection on 1/2/20 and 7/2/20.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed the large chest freezer in the storage area of the kitchen and the small chest freezer by the salad prep area to have accumulation of frost. Defrost freezers as needed. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed multiple to-go sauce cups as scoops in top prep coolers (cheese, diced herbs). Cease practice. Scoops should have a handle and be above the top of the food item. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at pizza prep area and dish drying area. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed several areas of facility (pizza prep area and dry dish area) where clean dishware and/or cookware was placed right-side up and thus not in protection from cross-contamination. Discussed flipping dished and pots over so food- and lip- contact surfaces are protected from contamination. This is a repeat violation since the last routine 
inspection on 1/2/20.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple fans. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed fan in cooler storage area (on floor) and two small fans in dry dish area to have accumulation of dust. Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/2/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be drying within the mop bucket. Mops should be hung in a manner that allows to drip and/or air dry. Discussed procedure with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/2/20.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Multiple areas were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable - in need of caulking. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed hand sink at customer bathrom (nearest kitchen) and hand sink near dish machine area to have caulk coming from the wall and sink. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

Observed facility to lack employee health reporting agreements signed by all food handlers. Observed no paperworking regarding proper exclusion and restriction of employees, as well as paperwork for the requirements of diagnosed food service employees. Provided paperwork to PIC and explained importance of documents. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

Observed employee to wash hands properly, but turn off faucet before drying hands with paper towels. Proper hand washing technique requires food handler to wash hands and turn off facuet after drying hands, using the paper towel in order to prevent cross-contamination. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11  (Pf) Food employee wet rags in hand sinks. Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed food handler twice to wet rags in two different hand sinks. Hand washing sinks are to be utilized for hand washing only. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11  (P) Tomatoes and other ready-to-eat foods stored below raw shell eggs. Store all ready-to-eat foods above raw shell eggs to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

Observed raw shell eggs to be stored above tomatoes and other ready-to-eat foods. Discussed storage order with PIC in order to hinder cross-contamination. Provided paperwork regarding importance of storage order, as well as correct food order in coolers. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Utensil trays (food contact surface) is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed multiple cooking utensil trays beneath prep table to have debris within the trays. Discussed routine cleaning of trays in order to prevent contamination of food-contact surfaces. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items within facility. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple items throughout facility to lack date marking. PIC indicated which items were to be utilized within 24 hours and which were in need of date marking. 
Items included:
1. 2 milk jugs within reach-in cooler #1
2. meatballs and sauce within shallow tray with aluminum foil covering tray in reach-in cooler #1
3. opened ham and sausage packages within reach-in cooler #2
4. pesto chicken within reach-in cooler #2

Discussed proper date marking and importance with PIC. Provided additional paperwork regarding rational for date marking and proper techniques. COS.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

Observed several items throughout facility to appear to have inadequate cooling.
Items included:
1. alfredo sauce within a large plastic container with lid in reach-in cooler #1 --> 141 degrees F (internal temp)
2. lasagna meat within Tupperware container with lid in reach-in cooler #2 --> 79 degrees F (internal temp)
3. meatballs within Tupperware container with lid in reach-in cooler near prep line --> 53 degrees F (internal temp)

Discussed various methods of cooling such as shallow trays and an ice bath method. Provided multiple papers regarding importance of proper cooling technique: 135 degrees F to 70 degrees F within 2 hours and from 70 degrees F to 41 degrees F within an additional 4 hours, 6 hours in total. Provided a cooling log for facility in order to maintain all items are adhering to proper cooling techniques. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed several areas of facility (dish rack in kitchen prep area, prep area dishes, clean pots in cooking utensil storage) where clean dishware and/or cookware was placed right-side up and thus not in protection from cross-contamination. Discussed flipping dishes and pots over so food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of chest freezers are no longer easily cleanable. Reference 4-101.19.

Observed all chest freezers to have a large accumulation of frost. Discussed routine cleaning of freezers to hinder frost accumulation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans near clean cooking utensils. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed both small fans above the clean cooking utensil racks near dish machine to have an accumulation of dust. Discussed routine cleaning of fans in order to deter dust.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13  (P) Waste water from mop bucket is being improperly disposed. All sewage discharge must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Reference 5-402.13.

Observed mop bucket to be containing waste water without proper disposal. Discussed with PIC routine disposal of mop bucket waste water in-between uses. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be within mop bucket and waste water. Mops must be hung in a way that allows for air drying and/or drip drying when in-between uses. COS.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Caulk of 3 compartment sink was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed caulk of 3 compartment sink to be peeling away and cracked; therefore, no longer smooth or easily cleanable. Discussed re-caulking with PIC.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-202.11  (C) Lighting was found not shielded or otherwise protected in the cooler area. Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Reference 6-202.11.

Observed one ceiling light to be unshielded within the hand sink and cooler area of kitchen. Discussed need for shielding all light bulbs within facility with PIC.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11  (P) A can of Raid bug killer was observed stored over the dish area. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the can moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed food employee shut off water value with bare hands after handwashing at hand sink in the kitchen area. Please use barrier to prevent recontamination of hands. 
->Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Importance of proper hand washing was discussed with staff. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
4 carton of raw eggs found stored with bags of argula and above lemons and oranges in domestic refrigerator across from the coffee bar in the back kitchen area.
->Store raw animal products away from ready to eat foods and by cooking temperature to protect from possible cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The following cold holding items were found improperly cold holding above 41F: 
In the 2 door make table cooler: Spinach 51F, argula 52F, romaine 44F -> All found in lidded containers. Lids removed for rapid cooling. 
->Ensure cold holding food items are maintained with temperatures at 41F or less. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Staff indicated Meguiar's brand Wheel and Tire cleaner (which was found hanging on shelf near dish machine) is used to remove carbon build-up on pots and pans. Please discussed use of chemicals which are not approved for food contact surfaces. 
Raid flying insect spray labeled for domestic/household use only found stored on shelf above dirty dish drain. Toxic was removed at the time of inspection. 
->Toxic materials that are not required for the operation and maintenance of a food establishment must be removed. Reference 7.202.11.
Unlabeled spray bottle of unknown liquid found stored on shelf above dirty drain board. Liquid was discarded and importance of labeling chemicals was discussed.
->Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. . Reference 7-102.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Wall mounted fan above shelving with clean utensils in the warewashing area found accumulated with dust and debris.
->Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed raw beef stored above spices in the cooler. 2) Observed raw meat stored above shrimp in the cooler. Both were stored in the correct manner to prevent potential cross contamination.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the chest freezer needing defrosted holding noodles in the kitchen. Defrost the chest freezer.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed an issue with the soap (not dispensing properly). The soap was corrected during the inspection and provided at the handwashing sink.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed eggplant date marked 08/22. 2) Observed the desserts in cooler measuring 49 F. The inspector told the operator to discard any leftover desserts after lunch. He stated he placed them into the cooler this morning. Do not place desserts in the cooler until it is measuring 41 F or below.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed bulk spices to have no labels. The labels were provided with the proper common name.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed beans date marked 5/3/18. Make sure to use or discard within seven days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
1) Observed cans of tomato sauce stored on the floor. 2) Observed shrimp uncovered in the prep cooler. Cover all foods.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed containers with no handles stored in the spices. Make sure to have the handle extended out the food or do not store containers in the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed multiple employee drinks stored on countertops. Make sure to keep lids and straws and drinks separate from food.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed dish machine to not have proper sanitizer hook up. Bleach was brought to the facility during the inspection. Sanitizer buckets were not set up correctly. Education was provided.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths stored on contact surfaces. Make sure to store cloths in the sanitizer buckets.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the can opener blade soiled. Make sure to clean all food contact surfaces as needed. 2) Observed the meat slicer to be soiled. Clean food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service items to be stored incorrectly. All single service items were inverted during the inspection.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed coving in the 220 building basement to be missing. Replace coving.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
